title: Band Generator Project
summary: Module project: a styled Band Name Generator built with Express and EJS. A POST route picks a random adjective and noun, passes them to the template, a conditional switches the heading, shared partials carry the CSS link and footer, and the footer shows the current year computed on the server.

concepts.heading: Project setup and target behaviour
points: Download and unzip the starter, run npm i, then launch the finished version with nodemon solution.js to view the target at localhost:3000.

Target: the home page shows a default welcome h1 and a Generate Name button. Each click posts a form and the page comes back with a new 'adjective noun' heading. The page is styled and its footer shows a copyright with the current year.
The starter index.js lists four numbered steps with hints. The work is split across index.js, views/index.ejs and the two partials.

concepts.heading: Step 1: render the home page
points: app.get("/") responds with res.render("index.ejs"). Test after every step: the default h1 and the button should appear.

concepts.heading: Step 2: random name generation and conditional heading
points: The button lives inside a form with action="/submit" and method="POST", so clicking it sends a POST to /submit. body-parser (app.use(bodyParser.urlencoded({ extended: true }))) is already wired in; this form carries no fields, so it is not strictly needed here.

Random pick from an array: arr[Math.floor(Math.random() * arr.length)]. Math.random() returns a decimal in [0, 1), multiplying by the length scales it to the index range, Math.floor drops the decimals to a valid integer index.
Do this once for the adj array and once for the noun array (both are long word lists at the bottom of the file).
Send the result to the template with local data: res.render("index.ejs", { adjective: randomAdj, noun: randomNoun }). The object's keys become variable names inside the EJS file.
In the template, print them with the escaped output tag: <%= adjective %> <%= noun %>, with a space between so the heading reads 'adjective noun'.

On first page load (GET) no data is passed, so referencing a bare adjective variable would throw a ReferenceError. Guard with a conditional using the scriptlet tag <% ... %>: if (locals.adjective && locals.noun) render the generated heading, else render the default heading.
locals is the object holding everything passed to render. Reading a property on it returns undefined instead of throwing, which makes it the safe way to test whether data was supplied.
Each line of JavaScript control flow needs its own EJS tag: <% if (...) { %>, <% } else { %>, <% } %>. HTML written between the tags is output only for the branch that runs.

(Extra) The reference repo's starter version of the file wraps the generator in a helper function and passes a single bandName key instead of two keys; the lecture's own version passes adjective and noun separately.

concepts.heading: Step 3: make the styling show up
points: CSS is a static file: place it at public/styles/main.css and register the folder with app.use(express.static("public")).
The stylesheet link goes in the head of the header partial. Its href is written from the point of view of the public folder: styles/main.css (a leading slash, /styles/main.css, is the safer form).

Pages must actually use the partials: add <%- include("partials/header.ejs") %> at the top of index.ejs and <%- include("partials/footer.ejs") %> at the bottom. Include paths are relative to the views folder.
Verify styling appears on both the initial GET page and the page rendered after the POST.

concepts.heading: Step 4: dynamic year in the footer
points: Hard-coded years in a copyright line go stale. Replace the placeholder year in the footer partial with <%= new Date().getFullYear() %>.

new Date() builds a Date for now and getFullYear() returns its four-digit year as a number. The output tag <%= %> prints the value into the page, while a plain <% %> tag would run the code and print nothing.
Because the code runs on the server each time the template is rendered, no client-side script is required.

task.name: Band Name Generator
task.starting_point: Zip containing index.js (routes missing, four commented steps with hints, adjective and noun arrays at the bottom), views/index.ejs and partials header.ejs/footer.ejs with comments marking where code goes, public/styles/main.css, and a finished solution.js with solution.ejs.
task.goal: A fully functional, styled generator: default heading on first visit, a random 'adjective noun' heading after each button click, and a footer with the current year.
steps: Step 1: add the GET / route that renders index.ejs.

Step 2: in the POST /submit route pick a random adjective and noun from the arrays, then render index.ejs with those values. In index.ejs show them in the h1 when present and show the default h1 otherwise.
Step 3: serve the public folder with express.static, link styles/main.css inside the header partial, and include the header and footer partials in index.ejs.
Step 4: replace the placeholder year in the footer partial with a server-computed current year using new Date().getFullYear().
Test each step in the browser at localhost:3000 before moving to the next.
task.expected_result: Visiting / shows the styled welcome heading and button. Clicking Generate Name shows a new random band name each time. The footer reads Copyright followed by the current year.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 25 - EJS/25.05 - Band Generator Project/solution.js (views/solution.ejs, views/partials/solution-header.ejs and solution-footer.ejs)

pitfalls: Accessing adjective or noun without the locals guard, which throws a ReferenceError on the initial GET.
Using <% %> where <%= %> is needed (nothing printed) or <%= %> for include (HTML escaped).
Forgetting the stylesheet link in the header partial, or not including the partials in index.ejs, so no styling shows.
Index maths: Math.floor(Math.random() * arr.length) must use the array length; using length - 1 would exclude the last item.
(Extra) The starter repo's index.js lists duplicate words in the arrays, and the student's footer partial carries a personal credit line that should be dropped when reusing it.
(Extra) Rendering directly from a POST means a browser refresh asks to resubmit the form; a redirect pattern avoids that but then needs another way to carry the data.

gaps_and_ideas: New lesson 'Band Name Generator (EJS project)': blurb on combining POST route, local data, conditional rendering and partials.

Tasks: (1) render the home page, (2) write a pickRandom(arr) helper and use it in POST /submit, (3) pass adjective and noun to render and show them with <%= %>, (4) wrap the heading in locals-based if/else, (5) add a footer partial with new Date().getFullYear().
Starter code idea: index.js with the two arrays and empty routes, index.ejs with a form and the default h1.

Interactive demo idea: a mock browser with a Generate button that animates the request: shows the POST, the data object passed to render, and which branch of the if/else was taken, with a toggle that removes the locals guard to display the resulting error.
